```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(plotly)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.asp = .55,
  out.width = "100%")

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
```

```{r noaa_import, include=FALSE}
data("ny_noaa")

noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  select(id, date, tmax, tmin, prcp) |>
  mutate(date_parts = date) |>
  separate(date_parts, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") |>
  mutate(
    month = as.numeric(month),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10) |>
  filter(year == "2010")

```

```{r noaa_summary, include=FALSE}
noaa_temperature_df =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(!is.na(tmax), !is.na(tmin), tmin <= tmax)

noaa_monthly_df =
  noaa_temperature_df |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(
    maximum = mean(tmax),
    minimum = mean(tmin)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    maximum:minimum,
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "temperature")

noaa_precipitation_df =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(!is.na(prcp)) |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarize(mean_prcp = mean(prcp))

noaa_scatter_df =
  noaa_temperature_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = c(1, 7), labels = c("January", "July")))
```

# Problem 2

## Temperature relationship {data-width=650}

### Daily minimum and maximum temperatures (January and July)

```{r noaa_scatter}
noaa_scatter_plot =
  noaa_scatter_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = month)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .25) +
  labs(
    x = "Daily minimum temperature (C)",
    y = "Daily maximum temperature (C)",
    color = "Month")

ggplotly(noaa_scatter_plot)
```

## Monthly summaries {data-width=350}

### Monthly mean daily temperatures

```{r noaa_monthly}
noaa_monthly_plot =
  noaa_monthly_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = temperature, color = measure)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Month (1 = January)",
    y = "Temperature (C)",
    color = "Daily measure") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly(noaa_monthly_plot)
```

### Mean daily precipitation by month

```{r noaa_precipitation}
noaa_precipitation_df |>
  rename(
    Month = month,
    `Mean daily precipitation (mm)` = mean_prcp) |>
  plot_ly(
    x = ~Month,
    y = ~`Mean daily precipitation (mm)`,
    type = "bar")
```

# Data and methods

## Data preparation

### Data source and preparation

The dataset is `ny_noaa` from p8105.datasets. The full course dataset covers New York weather station records from 1981 through 2010. This dashboard filters to 2010, which contains `r nrow(noaa_df)` station-day records from `r n_distinct(noaa_df$id)` stations. Each record describes one station on one date. The data are loaded from the package during knitting.

I use `separate()` to split dates into year, month, and day, and `mutate()` to convert month and temperatures to numeric values. Temperatures and precipitation are divided by 10 to convert the original tenths of a degree Celsius and tenths of a millimeter to degrees Celsius and millimeters.

#### Missing and inconsistent measurements

The temperature plots use the `r nrow(noaa_temperature_df)` records with both minimum and maximum temperatures observed and minimum no greater than maximum. This complete-pair restriction keeps the two monthly temperature means comparable. Records with missing temperatures or a minimum exceeding the maximum are removed from the temperature plots; they can still contribute to the precipitation plot.

Precipitation means exclude missing precipitation measurements and retain observed zeros. The precipitation plot therefore uses a different set of observations from the temperature plots. Missing values are never replaced by zero.

#### Plot types and data reduction

The dashboard contains three distinct plot types: a scatterplot, a line chart, and a bar chart. The scatterplot filters to January and July instead of randomly sampling observations, using all `r nrow(noaa_scatter_df)` eligible station-days in those two months. The line and bar charts summarize all eligible 2010 records by month using `group_by()` and `summarize()`. The two temperature lines use the same observations within each month. Bars show mean precipitation per observed station-day, rather than monthly rainfall totals.

Hover for values, click a legend to hide a series, or drag to zoom. Double-click to reset the view.

#### Interpretation

January and July temperature pairs form colder and warmer groups in the scatterplot. The monthly lines show the expected seasonal pattern, with higher temperatures during summer. Mean daily precipitation varies across months and is highest in October in these available records.

The summaries describe available station-days. Stations with more observed days receive more weight, and reporting coverage can vary across months and variables. These are not area-weighted statewide estimates. A single year does not establish a long-term climate trend.
